bull.b: Sustained high gross and operating margins indicate durable pricing power and favorable mix toward full‑price and higher‑margin channels. Margin strength supports reinvestment, shareholder returns and resilience to modest top‑line softness over the medium term.

Consistent, growing free cash flow gives the company financial flexibility to fund marketing, store expansion, buybacks and dividends without relying on new debt. Improved cash conversion supports capital allocation and cushions against cyclical retail volatility.

Robust DTC customer gains and elevated brand engagement strengthen a higher‑margin revenue channel and deepen customer data assets. This structural shift enhances lifetime value, pricing control and international digital expansion potential over multiple years.

bear.b: Meaningful leverage reduces financial flexibility and increases vulnerability to revenue shocks or rising interest costs. In a consumer cyclical industry, higher debt can constrain investment cadence, limit opportunistic M&A, and pressure cash returns during downturns.

bear.t: Europe macro pressure and softer store traffic
bear.b: Persistently weak European demand and tourism sensitivity can depress full‑price sell‑through and force higher promotional activity. Structural regional headwinds may require sustained marketing or price investments that compress margins and slow margin recovery.

bear.t: Wholesale/channel rationalization may dampen near‑term growth
bear.b: Strategic exits from lower‑tier wholesale and off‑price channels enhance brand control and long‑term margin but trade off near‑term volume and geographic reach. This structural rebalancing can reduce visible top‑line growth and create lumpy revenue cadence over multiple quarters.
